security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick findings are Markdown false positives, but several examples intentionally run the belt CLI and npx installers. The skill has real external command and network exposure because prompts, image URLs, and install commands can leave the reviewed package.

remediation.suggestion: Restrict allowed tools to the specific belt commands required for image generation, browsing, and upscaling. Require confirmation for login, install, or account-changing commands.

remediation.issue: Community install commands are not pinned
remediation.suggestion: Replace npx skill installation examples with pinned versions and clear manual review steps. Avoid recommending broad related-skill installs in the primary workflow.

remediation.issue: External data sharing is not disclosed
remediation.suggestion: Add a short privacy notice before examples that send prompts or image URLs to hosted providers. Warn users not to submit sensitive images.

remediation.issue: Remote documentation and media are hardcoded
remediation.suggestion: Prefer reviewed local setup notes or pinned trusted links. Remove remote tracking images when they are not required for the skill to work.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Belt CLI Permission
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows Bash(belt *), which permits any belt subcommand instead of only the image-generation commands shown in examples. This broad permission can affect account state or call remote services beyond the narrow workflow.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The allowed-tools front matter directly grants Bash access to every belt subcommand. The rest of the skill relies on belt for login, model discovery, and app execution.

content.user_title: Generate AI Images With Hosted Models
content.value_statement: Image teams need fast access to many generation models without learning each provider API. This skill gives repeatable belt CLI workflows for creation, editing, and upscaling.
actual_capabilities: Lists image-generation models available through inference.sh and the belt CLI.
Shows text-to-image examples for GPT-Image-2, FLUX, Gemini, Grok, Reve, and Seedream.
Documents image editing workflows that use prompts and existing image URLs.
Includes upscaling and image stitching examples for hosted image apps.
Points users to related image, video, avatar, and background removal skills.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI and an inference.sh account before commands can run.
Image prompts and image URLs may be sent to external providers.
Model names, prices, and availability can change outside this skill.
The skill provides workflows and commands, not a local image model.

use_cases.title: Create Marketing Visuals
use_cases.description: Generate campaign images, social graphics, and product concepts with model-specific prompts and aspect ratios.

use_cases.title: Prototype Product Shots
use_cases.description: Create studio-style product images, test backgrounds, and compare models before commissioning final assets.

use_cases.title: Build Image Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn repeatable image tasks into documented CLI steps for generation, editing, upscaling, and review.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to create an image from this prompt: [describe scene]. Recommend a model and aspect ratio.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to change this image: [image URL]. Keep the subject and adjust [background, style, or detail].

prompt_templates.title: Compare Models for a Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to compare GPT-Image-2, FLUX, and Seedream for [campaign]. Recommend settings, cost tradeoffs, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ai-image-generation to design a repeatable workflow for [product catalog]. Include model selection, prompt fields, review checks, and privacy notes.

output_examples.input: Generate a studio product image for a black ceramic mug.
output_examples.output: Recommended GPT-Image-2 for product detail, with a clean studio prompt, square aspect ratio, and human review before publishing.

output_examples.input: Change a portrait background to a sunset beach scene.
output_examples.output: Recommended an image editing model, a concise background prompt, and a reminder to avoid uploading private or licensed images.

output_examples.input: Upscale a generated poster for print review.
output_examples.output: Recommended the Topaz upscaler workflow, with source image checks and a final inspection for text accuracy.

best_practices: Use non-sensitive prompts and images unless your provider agreement allows that data.
Start with a simple prompt, then add style, lighting, aspect ratio, and quality details.
Review generated images for brand fit, licensing concerns, text errors, and unsafe content.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private product images into hosted models without approval.
Do not assume model pricing or availability is current without checking the provider.
Do not install related skills or CLIs without reviewing their source and permissions.

faq.question: What does this skill help me generate?
faq.answer: It helps generate, edit, upscale, and stitch images through hosted inference.sh image apps.

faq.question: Does it run a model locally?
faq.answer: No. It uses the belt CLI to call hosted image models and services.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it edit existing images?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes examples for image editing with prompts and image URLs.

faq.question: What should I check before using it?
faq.answer: Confirm belt CLI setup, account access, model availability, pricing, and data handling rules.

faq.question: Is this safe for confidential images?
faq.answer: Use caution. The workflows can send prompts and image URLs to external hosted providers.
